description: This is how softened butter, melted butter, and browned butter affect cookies! Can you believe that this is the same recipe and that the only thing I changed was the form of butter that I used? Both the softened butter and the softened browned butter resulted in cookies with more spreading and less browning than their melted butter counterparts. This can be because of the process of creaming butter and sugar together. Incorporating a lot of air into the cookies creates a cookie that is more insulated because air is an insulator. This prevents flour from cooking quickly in the oven, allowing the cookie to spread more and prevents browning.  For a longer video breakdown with more details on the differences and cookie science behind these results, check out my bio ❤️ I know you’re going to ask soooooo: I preferred the melted browned butter cookie the most because of the caramelized cookie and browned butter flavor. So good!  Produced with the participation of the @CMF / FMC  #cookies #cookiehacks
transcript: Here's how the form of butter that you add into cookies affects them. I made four batches of chocolate chip cookies. The only thing I changed in the recipe was the form of the butter. I test a softened butter, melted butter, browned melted butter and browned softened butter. I just cooled it down and stirred it until it was a softened butter consistency. The softened butter cookie dough turned out pale and creamy. It's a classic cookie dough. Melted butter made a cookie dough that was much darker. Butter is anywhere from 80 to 85% fat. So when you brown it, you get rid of about 10 to 15% of moisture. This resulted in a drier, almost crumbly cookie dough when I used melted brown butter and softened brown butter. They all got baked at the same temperature for the same amount of time. Softened butter had the thinnest cookie with the most amount of spread, with the softest, melty center and a classic chocolate chip cookie flavor. Melted butter had the second most amount of spread, a much thicker cookie and had the most amount of browning. It had much crispier edges and also had a caramelized cookie flavor. The middle was still soft, but not quite as soft as the softened butter. Melted brown butter had the least amount of spread, the thickest cookie and crisp all the way around the outside, not just the edges. The very center was still gooey and had a caramelized cookie and brown butter flavor. Softened brown butter cookies spread more than the previous, with the least amount of browning and a very crisp buttery exterior. It tasted like brown butter shortbread with a soft center. Which type of cookie do you prefer? And check out the caption for details on the science behind these results.
